chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Bukayr ibn A'yn and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ajli from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) who said:
Whoever buys a female slave who has a husband, then her sale is her divorce; if the buyer wishes, he separates them, and if he wishes, he leaves them upon their marriage.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of a female slave when she is sold to a new owner?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of the *mukatab* or married slave woman upon sale, establishing that the transaction itself acts as a revocable divorce (*taliq*) rather than an automatic dissolution. It grants the new owner (*sayyid*) the discretion to either maintain the marital bond within his household or separate the couple, reflecting the unique legal flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of the master over the slave's personal status. This ruling underscores the practical application of *ikhtiyar* (choice) in family law structures within the context of *milk al-yamin* (ownership of the right hand).
